title: Start Console responses without request-time runtime initialization
description:
As a Console user, I want the first response chunk promptly, so that interactive scorecard work feels responsive and predictable.

Feature: Interactive Console latency

Scenario: First request on a provisioned instance
Given a provisioned Console responder is ready
When a user sends a simple message
Then Tactus model infrastructure was already initialized
And the response records separate preparation, model initialization, provider first-chunk, and streaming timings
And the client receives the first chunk in approximately five seconds or less under normal provider conditions

Scenario: Supported integration only
Given Plexus runs a Tactus agent
When the agent executes
Then Plexus uses released public Tactus APIs
And does not replace Tactus private methods at runtime.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Sandbox latency verification found two repeatable request-time costs before provider dispatch: the model prewarm cache does not match the effective agent configuration, and a short Console turn performs an unnecessary remote mid-run steering lookup. The first visible response was 15.2s; server telemetry showed 5.3s agent preparation, request-time LM initialization, and 3.9s provider first chunk. Warm turns repeated 4.2-4.6s preparation and request-time LM initialization. Fixing both before dependency publication and rerunning the benchmark.
